title: DCF, Multiples & Quick Valuation Math
description: Practice rapid valuation reasoning using DCF mechanics, trading multiples, and investment sizing under time pressure.

interactions.prompt: A SaaS company has $80M ARR growing 40% YoY, 75% gross margins, and trades at 18x revenue. Comparable peers at similar growth trade at 25x. What's the key signal?

options.text: Growth rate is unsustainable at 40%
The stock is ~28% undervalued vs. growth-matched peers
Gross margins are too high to be credible
Revenue multiple is already stretched at 18x

interactions.prompt: A firm generates $50M FCF growing at 5% perpetually with a 10% WACC. Its terminal value is $____ million.
You're sizing a Series B investment. Company A: $20M ARR, 90% net retention, 30x multiple but needs $60M. Company B: $35M ARR, 110% net retention, 20x multiple, needs $40M. You have $50M to deploy.

options.text: Invest in A  -  higher growth ceiling justifies premium
Invest in B  -  superior retention and cheaper entry
Split $25M into each for diversification
Pass on both  -  neither shows capital efficiency

interactions.prompt: Uber's 2019 IPO: $14B revenue, -$8.5B operating loss, priced at ~$75B. Lyft at $3.6B revenue, -$0.9B loss, priced at ~$20B. Uber had 65% US rideshare. What matters most for the valuation gap?

options.text: Uber's diversified business lines justified a platform premium
Lyft was actually cheaper on a revenue multiple basis
Both were equally overvalued given operating losses
Market share alone explains the entire difference

chartData.title: Uber vs Lyft 2019 IPO Metrics Comparison

interactions.prompt: Rank these DCF assumptions by their impact on a high-growth tech company's valuation, from MOST to LEAST sensitive.

options.text: Terminal growth rate (3% vs. 5%)
Revenue growth rate years 1-5 (25% vs. 35%)
WACC (9% vs. 12%)
Long-term operating margin (20% vs. 25%)

interactions.prompt: You're valuing a pre-profit marketplace. Your DCF gives $2.4B, EV/GMV comps suggest $1.6B, and a recent acquisition of a peer implies $3.1B. Management wants the highest defensible number for fundraising.

options.text: Use $3.1B  -  transaction comps reflect actual willingness to pay
Use $2.4B  -  DCF captures your specific unit economics
Use $1.6B  -  conservative builds investor trust
Triangulate at ~$2.4B weighting DCF and transaction comp higher

interactions.prompt: You're selecting comparable companies for valuing a $500M-revenue B2B cybersecurity firm. Rank these comp criteria from MOST to LEAST important for accurate multiples.

options.text: Similar revenue growth trajectory and guidance
Same industry sub-sector (endpoint vs. cloud security)
Comparable revenue scale ($300M - $800M range)
Similar margin profile and Rule of 40 score

interactions.prompt: Interest rates just jumped 200bps and your target's customers are mid-market enterprises now delaying software purchases. How does your valuation thesis change?

options.text: WACC rises ~2%, but near-term growth slows more  -  double hit to DCF
Higher rates don't matter for high-growth  -  maintain original valuation
Only discount rate changes; revenue assumptions stay intact
Switch entirely to asset-based valuation instead of DCF

interactions.priorContext: You previously valued the B2B cybersecurity firm at $5.2B using a 10% WACC and 30% revenue growth. Macro conditions have now shifted dramatically.
